CodeChallenge.description: CodeChallenge is a sign-in waiting for its emailed code, as the page shows it.

attempts_left.description: `attempts_left` is how many more codes may be typed before this sign-in is spent and has to be started again.

email.description: `email` is masked: enough to recognise one's own address, not to learn someone else's.

handle.description: `handle` names the sign-in. The page keeps it and sends it back.

resend_after.description: `resend_after` is seconds until another code may be sent, for a countdown.

CodeRequest.description: codeRequest is the body of POST /account/login/code: the handle the sign-in was held under, and the code from the message.

ConnectedApplication.description: ConnectedApplication is an application that can still act for the user: one holding a refresh token for them.

DiscoverRequest.description: discoverRequest is the address "Sign in with SSO" looks a connection up by.

email.description: An email address, at most 255 characters.

Discovery.description: Discovery is the OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 document.

op_tos_uri.description: The organisation's terms and privacy links (op_tos_uri, op_policy_uri), omitted when unset.

service_documentation.description: `service_documentation` links developers to the project's documentation.

EmailRequest.description: emailRequest is the body of POST /account/email: the address to move to.

current_password.description: `current_password` proves the person at the session owns the account; a wrong one counts towards the lockout, as at sign-in. At most 128 characters.

email.description: An email address, at most 255 characters.

ErrorResponse.description: errorResponse is an OAuth error (RFC 6749 section 5.2).

ForgotRequest.description: forgotRequest is the body of POST /account/forgot-password.

email.description: An email address, at most 255 characters.

language.description: `language` is the one the page was shown in, which the email is written in. One that is not offered, or none, is the default. At most 16 characters.

JWK.description: JWK is a public key as a JSON Web Key (RFC 7517).

JWKS.description: JWKS is the JSON Web Key Set.

LoginRequest.description: loginRequest is the body of POST /account/login. Request is the handle of the sign-in under way, when there is one.

remember.description: `remember` is the "stay signed in" box. A flow that does not offer it ignores whatever is sent.

OAuthError.description: An OAuth 2.0 error (RFC 6749 section 5.2), which is how the provider's own endpoints answer.

PasswordRequest.description: passwordRequest is the body of POST /account/password.

Problem.description: An error the API answers with. `code` is stable, and what an application should act on; `error` is its English sentence; `params` fills in the sentence's {placeholders}.

ProfileRequest.description: profileRequest is the body of PATCH /account/me.

PublicApplication.description: PublicApplication is what anyone may know about an application: what its sign-in pages show.

PublicLanguage.description: PublicLanguage is one language in the picker: its code and its English and native names.

PublicLoginOptions.description: PublicLoginOptions is the part of a flow the sign-in pages are told: what they may offer, and nothing about how the server checks any of it.

allow_email_change.description: `allow_email_change` offers "change" beside the address on the account page.

allow_remember_me.description: `allow_remember_me` puts "stay signed in" beside the password.

allow_sign_in.description: `allow_sign_in` false is a closed door: the pages say so instead of asking for anything.

steps.description: `steps` are the steps that will actually run, in order; planned steps are left out.

PublicOrganization.description: PublicOrganization is what the sign-in pages show about the organisation. It is built by hand because anyone can read it.

timezone.description: `timezone` is the zone the pages say dates in.

RegisterRequest.description: registerRequest is the body of POST /account/register.

email.description: An email address, at most 255 characters.

RequestResponse.description: requestResponse is a sign-in under way, as the sign-in page shows it.

ResendRequest.description: resendRequest is the body of POST /account/login/code/resend.

SSOButton.description: SSOButton is a connection as a sign-in page offers it.

SessionInfo.description: SessionInfo is one browser a user is signed in on.

current.description: `current` marks the session the request itself carries.

SignedInResponse.description: signedInResponse says what the page does next: follow RedirectTo, choose a new password with ResetToken (temporary password), or ask for the emailed Code. With none, the user is signed in and there is nowhere to go.

SocialButton.description: SocialButton is a provider as a sign-in page shows it.

TokenResponse.description: TokenResponse is a successful token response (RFC 6749 section 5.1).

UserResponse.description: userResponse is built by hand so new columns, roles and organisation fields are never published to the user by accident.

VerifyRequest.description: resetRequest is the body of POST /account/reset-password. verifyRequest is the body of POST /account/verify-email.

accessToken.description: An access token this server issued.

accountToken.description: A user's access token for the account API (audience urn:loginer:account-api), with account.read to read and account.write to change.

clientSecretBasic.description: An application's client_id and client_secret, form-encoded and then base64-encoded (RFC 6749 section 2.3.1). The same credentials may be sent in the form instead.

userSession.description: A user's session at the provider, set by signing in on the sign-in pages.
userSession.name: loginer_user_session
